claim: A compact historical-propensity and persistence model is competitive with the full matched flexible predictor on held participants
prior_art: Source feedback/attitudinal effects and standard history/persistence accounts are known; no novel cognitive law
falsification: Advantage over flexible is small and its group-resampling interval must be checked; causal interpretation not identified
scope: Same seven repeated-lottery experiment designs; participant-held sequential history access

claim: Prospective feedback or visible-outcome learning alone does not reproduce the predictive benefit of prior-choice history
prior_art: Competing source-study accounts; numerical sufficiency rather than causal adjudication
falsification: A richer properly causal learning model or new participants/design may change the ranking
scope: Only tested families and input budget
